```{python}
#| label: imports
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from plotnine import *
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
```


```{python}
#| label: load-data
df = pd.read_csv('./data/run_time.csv')

# Melt from wide to long format
df_long = df.melt(id_vars='aligner', var_name='read_length', value_name='time_seconds')

# Extract numeric read length (e.g. '30_bp_s' -> 30)
df_long['read_length'] = df_long['read_length'].str.extract(r'(\d+)').astype(int)
df_long['read_length'] = pd.Categorical(df_long['read_length'], categories=sorted(df_long['read_length'].unique()))

print(df_long.head(10))
```

```{python}
#| label: plot
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6

grey_shades = ['#d9d9d9', '#bdbdbd', '#969696', '#636363', '#252525']

p = (
    ggplot(df_long, aes(x='aligner', y='time_seconds', fill='factor(read_length)'))
    + geom_col(position=position_dodge(width=0.8), width=0.7)
    + scale_fill_manual(values=grey_shades)
    + labs(
        title='Aligner run times by read length (5 million reads/length)',
        x='Aligner',
        y='Wall-clock time (seconds)',
        fill='Read length (bp)',
    )
    + theme_bw()
    + theme(
        axis_text_x=element_text(angle=35, hjust=1),
        figure_size=(10, 6),
    )
)

p.save('runtime.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
p
```
